title: metadata-protocol: reverting a revert commit restores nothing (its items carry prevVersion null), against ADR-0067 D3
body:
domain:skills#1 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5pjSPT7ui2EUcunaVb

Filing gate: ① (a defect found by the at-tier contract review 6886701800 of PR #33465, card #32504; code outside that diff).

**What is wrong.** `revertCommit` in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` restores an item only when it has a `prevVersion` (or deletes it when it did not exist before). An item with `existedBefore: true` and no `prevVersion` takes neither branch and lands in neither `reverted[]` nor `failed[]`. Every revert commit records its restored items with `prevVersion: null`, and `readRevertableCommit` accepts revert commits. So reverting a revert silently restores nothing and reports nothing. ADR-0067 D3 promises an append-only history where a revert is itself revertible, and the `protocol.ts` docblock says "itself revertible".

**What lands.** Either record the version a revert replaced (so a revert commit carries a real `prevVersion`) and make revert-of-revert restore, or refuse a revert commit at `readRevertableCommit` by name and amend D3. Name the skipped outcome in the result either way. Pin it with a revert-of-revert test.

Related: #32504 / PR #33465 (the ADR-0067 amendment names this outcome or leaves it undecided).
